answer: Executor-invented ids/text are self-consistent: goldens are generated from the same fixture run, so any content works as long as the stated counts (2 tasks, 2 atoms, 1 pill, 1 drawer task) hold. No owner decision.

Both converge: scaffold_desk writes only missing files via _write_if_missing (deskops/workspace.py:194,259-261), so a hand-authored golden_desk/ is preserved and `desk install` can only add absent files. Hand-authoring the fixture is fine.

No store is needed. build_graph_snapshot only globs Markdown (deskops/graph/snapshot.py:59-98; extract_docs.py:52-113); tests run it on a bare tmp_path (tests/test_graph_snapshot.py:16-39), and write_graph_snapshot mkdirs .sldb/runtime/graphs itself (snapshot.py:108-113).

Already stated: Resolved Decisions mandates git init + one seed commit, and the named helper _make_repo also sets user.email/user.name (tests/test_lifecycle_end_to_end.py:36-44). closeout commit needs git identity, not a prior commit.

Helpers are module-local, not shared: _make_repo/_cli live in tests/test_lifecycle_end_to_end.py:22,36 and _make_repo is duplicated in tests/test_closeout.py:26; no conftest.py exists anywhere. Reimplement or import; conftest.py will hold only --update-golden.

Only the git commit sha is volatile: kg.json/self-findings carry relative paths and no timestamps (snapshot.py:113 sort_keys+newline; self_reflection.py:118), run-index keys are fixed (closeout.py:100-107). So <ts>/<root> are no-ops; regex choice is implementer-level.

Session-Sha256 is sha256 of the session file (closeout.py:157-160), so a fixed fixture yields a stable value; no normalization needed. It appears only when run.yaml/--session supplies it (closeout.py:170-174); the volatile value is the run_index commit sha.
Help text is static (build_parser sets only prog/description/epilog, parser.py:25-31; no --version), so normalizing it is a harmless no-op. Whether to apply it uniformly is an implementer choice.
route labels are not in code (closeout.py emits git trailers, not JSON); the golden is produced by the same run, so any labels/order are self-consistent. Implementer-level choice.

Any ids work: closeout commit never reads the task doc; --task only becomes the Task-Id trailer (closeout.py:82,170). No CLI makes run dirs, so hand-build runs/subagents/<dir> with board.txt, task.txt, git-status.txt, result-summary.md (closeout.py:24,131; tests/test_closeout.py:37-43).

No hidden or alias subparsers: parser.py has no argparse.SUPPRESS/aliases (grep empty); max depth is 2 (only parser.py:32 top-level plus per-command add_subparsers). Walk the parser tree or parse `deskops --help`; either works.

No beyond-depth-2 rule is needed: every add_subparsers call is top-level (parser.py:32) or a second-level command group (parser.py:66,114,313,358,382,397,469,571,661,845,870,930,977,1047,1069); max depth is 2.
Implementer-level: the task already says --update-golden `rewrites them`; rewriting all goldens (creating the directory as needed, exit 0) is the sane default. No owner decision.
Not needed: the test compares live output against the committed golden, so a regression to empty or renamed keys fails it; Done When's manual snapshot-key rename check is the anti-triviality guard.

No canonicalization needed: kg.json/self-findings use json.dumps(sort_keys=True)+newline (snapshot.py:113; self_reflection.py:118), run-index key order is fixed (closeout.py:100-107), nx.json node order follows the sorted snapshot (../sldb/src/sldb/store/graph/graph_io.py:19-24).
Generic process: recording an evidence note for the hand check is desk-closeout policy (AGENTS.md), not a task-specific decision. Done When already prescribes check-by-hand-then-revert.

All 9 depends_on tasks are unfinished (status: deferred at line 3 of each desk/drawer/tasks file, e.g. task-rw-f0-close-only-own-primitives.md:3). This task is itself status: deferred and not routed on desk/tasks/Board.md, so promote before execution.

Yes, same tmp copy: _graph_reflect reads default_snapshot_read_path(root) (deskops/cli/main.py:317-322), the snapshot graph build wrote under that root, and errors if it is absent. Run reflect after build in one root.
pytest tmp_path is per-test, so a shared module-level helper gives each test a fresh tmp copy. Standard test hygiene, no owner decision.
